subject: psychology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In Asch's line-judgement study, what did participants have to do?
options: Memorise a list of words in order
Decide whether to administer electric shocks
Estimate movement of a stationary light
Match a standard line to one of three comparison lines
questions.explain: Asch's task required participants to judge which of three comparison lines matched a standard line, with confederates giving wrong answers.

questions.q: 'Social cryptomnesia' in social change refers to what?
options: Forgetting the source of a now-accepted idea while remembering the change
A failure of retrieval cues in memory
questions.explain: Social cryptomnesia is when people recall that a social change occurred but forget how or who brought it about.

questions.q: Which of these is a verbal prod used by the experimenter in Milgram's study?
options: 'You will be paid extra to stop'
questions.explain: Standardised prods such as 'The experiment requires that you continue' were used to encourage obedience.

questions.q: In Milgram's proximity variation where the teacher forced the learner's hand onto a shock plate, obedience fell to roughly what level?
questions.explain: In the touch-proximity condition obedience dropped to about 30% as the consequences became unavoidable.

questions.q: Why is flexibility important for a minority alongside consistency?
options: It increases the size of the minority
It makes the minority appear dogmatic and rigid
It removes the need for commitment
It avoids the minority being seen as inflexible and unreasonable
questions.explain: Some flexibility prevents a minority appearing rigid and helps it be seen as reasonable, aiding persuasion.

questions.q: Why was Zimbardo's study terminated after only six days?
options: Guards' abuse and prisoners' distress became extreme
questions.explain: The study ended early because guards became increasingly brutal and several prisoners showed severe emotional breakdowns.

questions.q: According to agency theory, the 'agentic state' refers to acting as what?
options: An instrument carrying out another's wishes
questions.explain: In the agentic state a person sees themselves as an agent executing the orders of an authority figure, not responsible for their actions.

questions.q: Deeper processing of a minority's message is thought to lead to internalisation through which mechanism?
questions.explain: Minority influence encourages deeper thinking (validation), and committed minorities benefit from the augmentation principle leading to conversion.

questions.q: In Milgram's variations, obedience fell to about 47.5% when which situational variable changed?
options: The teacher and learner were in the same room
The study moved from Yale to a run-down office
The experimenter wore a lab coat
questions.explain: Relocating to a rundown office reduced the perceived legitimacy of the setting, lowering obedience to about 47.5%.

questions.q: Which of the following is a key feature of the authoritarian personality according to Adorno?
options: Submissiveness to authority and hostility to those of lower status
questions.explain: Authoritarian individuals show extreme respect for authority and contempt for those perceived as socially inferior.

questions.q: The shift from feeling personally responsible to acting on behalf of an authority is known as what?
questions.explain: The agentic shift is the move from the autonomous state to the agentic state when confronted by authority.

questions.q: Conforming because we want to be liked and accepted by a group is driven by which influence?
questions.explain: Normative social influence is the desire to be accepted and avoid rejection, leading to compliance with group norms.

questions.q: In the Stanford prison experiment, participants were assigned to roles by what method?
questions.explain: Zimbardo randomly allocated the mentally healthy volunteers to the roles of guard or prisoner.

questions.q: Moscovici's blue-green slide study primarily investigated which process?
questions.explain: Moscovici examined how a consistent minority could influence a majority's judgements of slide colour.

questions.q: Which type of conformity involves a genuine private change in belief that is the deepest and most permanent?
questions.explain: Internalisation is a true conversion of private beliefs, making it the deepest and most lasting form of conformity.

questions.q: In Milgram's original obedience study, what was the maximum voltage participants could administer?
questions.explain: The shock generator went up to 450 volts, and 65% of participants administered this maximum level.

questions.q: Looking to others for the correct answer in an ambiguous situation reflects which explanation of conformity?
questions.explain: Informational social influence occurs when we accept others' views as correct because we are unsure and want to be right.

questions.q: Zimbardo's Stanford prison experiment primarily investigated conformity to what?
questions.explain: The SPE examined how readily people conform to assigned social roles such as guard and prisoner.

questions.q: Which factor has been shown to help people resist obedience and conformity?
options: The presence of a disobedient or dissenting model
questions.explain: Social support from a disobedient model or dissenter makes it easier for individuals to resist pressure.

questions.q: In Asch's variations, what happened to conformity when the task was made more difficult?
questions.explain: Greater task difficulty increases ambiguity, raising informational social influence and therefore conformity.

questions.q: What percentage of Milgram's participants administered the full 450-volt shock?
questions.explain: 65% of participants continued to the maximum 450-volt shock despite the learner's apparent distress.

questions.q: People with an internal locus of control are generally more likely to do what?
questions.explain: Internals believe they control their own behaviour and so are better able to resist conformity and obedience.

questions.q: 'Legitimacy of authority' as an explanation for obedience refers to which idea?
options: We obey because of inherited personality traits
We obey only when threatened with punishment
We obey to be liked by peers
We obey those we perceive to have rightful social power
questions.explain: We are more likely to obey people we accept as having legitimate, socially agreed authority over us.

questions.q: Adorno argued the authoritarian personality originates largely from what?
questions.explain: Adorno linked the authoritarian personality to harsh, punitive parenting that produces displaced hostility onto weaker others.

questions.q: Which behavioural style is most important for a minority to exert influence, according to Moscovici?
questions.explain: A consistent minority that maintains the same position over time and between members is most persuasive.

questions.q: Adorno's authoritarian personality is measured using which scale?
questions.explain: Adorno developed the F-scale (fascism scale) to measure authoritarian personality traits.

questions.q: In Asch's study, conformity dropped sharply when one confederate gave the correct answer. This shows the effect of what?
questions.explain: A dissenting confederate broke the group's unanimity, providing social support and reducing conformity dramatically.

questions.q: Publicly agreeing with a group to gain approval while privately disagreeing is best described as which type of conformity?
questions.explain: Compliance is a superficial, temporary public change without private acceptance of the group's view.

questions.q: The process by which a minority view gradually becomes the majority view is known as what?
questions.explain: The snowball effect describes minority ideas spreading until they are widely adopted and become the new norm.

questions.q: Locus of control, as a concept relevant to resisting social influence, was proposed by whom?
questions.explain: Julian Rotter proposed the concept of locus of control, distinguishing internal from external control.
